approach: Add a pure module crates/athena-core/src/scope_guard.rs with input structs (AttemptRecord, RequestRecord), line grouping by union-find over retry_of and quotes links, named threshold constants, one function per signal T1..T5, and an evaluate_before_attempt(line, forecast_p90) that returns all five results. Tests replay the four section 5.1 cases from hand-built records. Then flip D127 to accepted in decisions.md, update scope-guard.md status, section 8 and section 13, and add a CHANGELOG entry. No I/O, no clock, no wiring.

decisions.choice: Signal results use enums: Level {None, Flag, Pause} for T1, T2, T3 and T5, and T4 returns Match {No, Maybe, Yes}, mapped to None, Flag, Pause.
decisions.reason: Section 5 gives flag and pause effects, and T4 'maybe' must flag without pausing. Enums make the cut A and speedup assertions direct.

rejected.why: Cannot express flag versus pause or the T4 maybe.

decisions.choice: T4 compares normalised unmet-criterion text (lower case, ASCII digits removed, whitespace collapsed) for the last two rejections of the line. Equal text gives Yes. One text containing the other, or sharing a majority of words, gives Maybe. Anything else, or a missing criterion on either, gives No or Maybe respectively (missing text is Maybe).
decisions.reason: This is the section 5 rule, with an unclear match flagged not paused. The Maybe rule is deliberately simple and is named in a doc comment.

rejected.why: That is T1 and cannot be told from cut A. The same-criterion rule would not exist to remove.
More code and tuning for a model's job (section 6).

decisions.choice: Time, spend and forecast p90 are fields on the input structs or arguments. No clock, no fs, no process.
decisions.reason: Criterion 4. The later watcher (job 5) supplies the values from records.

rejected.why: Couples the pure module to I/O types, and the shape of per-line cost is the open question that job 1 settles.

decisions.choice: Evaluate 'before attempt n' by passing the finished attempts only and reading T1 as: finished attempts >= 2, meaning the 3rd is about to be dispatched.
decisions.reason: Matches 'T1: 3rd attempt about to be dispatched' and the table's 'fires before attempt 3'.

rejected.option: Count the pending attempt in the input
rejected.why: Invents a record that does not exist yet.

decisions.choice: Docs: D127 status becomes accepted with a line naming 'the brain under Sri's delegation (BRIEF.md addenda of 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-25)' and the two changes. In scope-guard.md, section 8 'Goes to Sri' is reworded so escalations go to whoever holds Sri's delegation, with Sri only for what the brief reserves to Sri. Section 13 build order starts with jobs 1 and 5 (rules only) before 2 and 7 (value scoring and model scorer).
decisions.reason: This is exactly what the request asks.

rejected.why: Other text refers to job numbers. Add an order note and keep the numbers.

files.purpose: Pure line grouping, threshold constants, T1 to T5 functions, evaluate function and replay tests. Doc comments cite scope-guard.md sections.
Add `pub mod scope_guard;` in alphabetical order after `scoring`.
D127 title and status accepted, decider, the two changes.
Status line, section 8 'Goes to Sri' wording, section 13 build order (jobs 1 and 5 first).

steps: Create scope_guard.rs: constants, Verdict, AttemptRecord (attempt, verdict, unmet_criterion, cost_cents, agent_minutes, plan_files, plan_steps, planning_round), RequestRecord (id, retry_of, quotes), group_lines (union-find), Level, T4Match.
Implement t1 to t5 and normalise_criterion, plus evaluate_before_attempt that returns a Signals struct with a pause/flag summary. Add doc comments that cite section 5.
Write replay tests for the trailer, speedup, prompt-budget and cut A cases, grouping tests, normalisation and maybe tests, and the T4 different-criterion test.
Edit D127 in decisions.md, then the scope-guard.md status line, section 8 and section 13, then the CHANGELOG entry.
Run cargo fmt, clippy with -D warnings, and cargo test --locked.

risks.risk: Docs tests such as the boundary scan or budget tests may fail on the edited docs.
risks.mitigation: Avoid banned words and email-like text, and run cargo test --locked.

risks.risk: Tests that only assert types, or a T4 test that passes with the rule removed.
risks.mitigation: Include a different-criteria case and a same-criterion case with differing numbers, so both always-true and always-false mutations fail.

risks.risk: Floating-point threshold edges, such as 1.5 times p90.
risks.mitigation: Compare in integer cents or use >= on f64 values chosen to avoid ties, and test the boundary.

risks.risk: decisions.md is large (248 KB) and a doc budget test may count it.
risks.mitigation: Edit only the D127 block in place and keep the additions short.

demonstrations.method: Run the module's unit tests. They include tests named trailer_*, speedup_*, prompt_budget_* and cut_a_*, each building records and asserting the signals per evaluation point. Speedup: after attempt 1 no T4, after attempt 2 T4 is Pause, T1 and T3 flag, T5 flags then pauses by cumulative minutes. Cut A: T1 flag, T4 not Pause, no signal at Pause level. Prompt-budget: T5 Flag at 60 minutes and none at 59.
demonstrations.observes: All scope_guard tests pass, and the asserted levels match the section 5.1 table.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the signal functions, the evaluation points would not give the asserted levels (for example no T4 Pause after the 2nd speedup rejection).

demonstrations.method: Test t4_different_criteria_does_not_pause builds two rejections with different unmet criteria and asserts T4 is not Pause. The speedup test asserts Pause on two same-criterion rejections (with differing numbers). If the comparison is deleted or always true, one of the two tests fails.
demonstrations.observes: Both T4 tests pass. Making the comparison always true fails the different-criteria test, and always false fails the speedup test.
demonstrations.fails_without: The different-criteria test fails if the same-criterion comparison is removed or always true.

demonstrations.method: Read scope_guard.rs: the grouping function with a test that a request, its retry and a quoting request form one line and an unrelated request does not. The normalisation test covers case and numbers (for example 'Under 7 minutes' vs 'under 12 MINUTES' are Yes). A Maybe test confirms the flag-only effect. The constants include T1_ATTEMPT=3, T2_RATIO=1.5, T2_PLANNING_ROUND=3, T3_FLAG_RATIO=1.0, T3_PAUSE_RATIO=1.5, T3_LINE_DOLLARS=5.0, T4_REJECTIONS=2, T5_FLAG_MINUTES=60 and T5_PAUSE_MINUTES=120.
demonstrations.observes: The grouping, normalisation and maybe tests pass, and the constants are visible in the source.
demonstrations.fails_without: The grouping test would fail if the quote or retry links were ignored, and the maybe test would fail if a maybe paused.

demonstrations.method: Inspect the source for forbidden APIs, and confirm the export line.
demonstrations.observes: It compiles with `pub mod scope_guard;` in lib.rs. Reading the file shows no use of std::fs, std::process, std::net, SystemTime, Instant or any network crate. Time and spend are struct fields.

Clippy is clean. `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo test --locked` also pass, which includes the boundary and policy scan tests over the changed docs.

open_questions: The T4 'maybe' rule (containment or majority-word overlap) is a producer choice, since the design only says 'unclear'.
Whether a rejected attempt with no recorded unmet criterion counts as maybe is assumed, not stated in the design.
The cut A and trailer per-attempt figures are even splits, as section 5.1 says; the cut A criteria text is invented for the tests.
